subject: Discovery Recap: Finly - p95 latency & concurrency requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Joe Nguyen <joe@finly.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Discovery Recap: Finly - p95 latency & concurrency requirements

Joe / Anya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. Let me know if I missed anything.

Summary of what we heard
- Primary pain: inconsistent interactive chat experience during market open windows. Users report long stalls and degraded streaming UX (partial tokens appear slowly or drop).
- Current stack: Finly routes user chat to a hybrid setup (OpenAI-hosted for non-sensitive flows, plus a self-hosted LLM for higher-sensitivity flows). You use LangChain + a lightweight request broker and a Redis cache for prefix caching. No dedicated inference pool today — requests go to shared hosted endpoints and some self-hosted GPUs.
- Observed impact: tail latency spikes (p95) in the 1.2–1.8s range for streaming first-byte and often >2s for some completions during bursts; this is causing poor UX and lower conversion.

Success criteria (what success looks like)
- Streaming first-byte p95 <= 350ms for interactive chat (for typical 256–512 token prompts).
- End-to-end completion p95 <= 1s for most flows; allow a longer tail for large generations but target <1.5s for 512-token completions.
- Support sustained concurrency: 200 concurrent streaming sessions with ability to absorb short spikes to 500 concurrent sessions for up to 2 minutes without degraded p95.
- No token loss on reconnects; reconnect/resume behavior consistent with best-practice streaming UX.

Current constraints / assumptions
- Model: Finly is testing open-weights models similar in size to Llama2-13B / other 7–13B variants. Quantization and batching strategies are not yet standardized across teams.
- Network: regional users in US East (primary) — want local inference where possible.
- Budget: constrained — they prefer configuration suggestions that reduce per-token cost while meeting p95 targets.

Proposed next steps
1) We’ll run a focused perf plan — Marissa will share a lightweight perf-requirements doc and a short telemetry capture template (attached).
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Redwood infra + Finly platform team (suggest Tue Mar 23, 10am ET) to walk throughput patterns, QPS, and sample traces.
3) Redwood will propose an architecture: dedicated inference pool + streaming-first runtime (prefix caching + continuous batching) and an initial quantization/batching profile for Finly’s model family.
4) Run a 2-week POC with a small dedicated pool (controlled capacity) and baseline tests against your telemetry.

Attachments: finly_performance_requirements.pdf (short perf template), finly_telemetry_snippets.zip (sample traces you shared during the call).

Questions for you (so we can prep the deep-dive)
- Can you share representative QPS/connection patterns for a typical market open (CSV or telemetry link)?
- Are there any hard constraints on first-byte latency vs completion latency (i.e., is first-token latency more valuable to UX than end-to-end)?
- Any regulatory constraints for the specific customer cohort we should flag for Private/Dedicated deployment?

Thanks — I’ll follow up with calendar invites and the perf plan.
—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
https://redwood.ai
From: Joe Nguyen <joe@finly.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anya Patel <anya@finly.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Finly - p95 latency & concurrency requirements

Marissa — thanks for the thorough recap. Nothing major to add, just a few specifics to help prioritize: 

Quick clarifications
- Current telemetry (attached link) shows first-byte p95 ~1.5s during market open and completion p95 ~2.4s for 512-token flows. Our UX team flags first-byte stalls as the most visible problem.
- Concurrency: baseline sustained concurrent streaming sessions ~200 during market open, with short spikes to ~450–500 for 1–3 minute bursts (we see this every new feature release or market event).
- Throughput: average QPS is ~60, 95th-percentile QPS during spikes hits ~320.

Hard targets from product/ops
- First-byte p95 target: <= 400ms (critical for interactive feel).
- Completion p95 target (512 tokens): <= 1s (stretch goal, okay to be 1–1.5s during sustained highest load).
- We need a plan that keeps cost predictable — if Dedicated is required for consistency, we’ll need a sizing + cost estimate.

I’ve attached a short telemetry dump and a sample trace. Also, here are two items to help you prep:
- Telemetry: https://drive.finly.com/telemetry/finly_open_20260320.json
- Internal notes: "market-open-patterns.md" (we can share after NDA if needed)

Happy to run the deep-dive on Tue Mar 23 — 10am ET works for us.
—
Joe Nguyen
Head of Product, Finly
joe@finly.com
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 09:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Finly - p95 latency & concurrency requirements

Thanks both — I’ll own the POC plan from our side. Action items I’ll take before Tue: 

- Draft perf test plan and perf harness (we’ll include your telemetry patterns, Joe) and a list of tests: first-byte latency, steady-state throughput, burst soak to 500 concurrent streams, reconnect/resume tests.
- Quick cost estimate for a small Dedicated pool (GPU sizing + expected token/unit costs) and a Hosted fallback plan.
- Invite infra (Rishi Malhotra) and runtime lead (Vivek Kulkarni) to the Tue deep-dive.

Marissa — can you add a HubSpot deal link and the Finly contact details in the invite? I’ll attach the perf plan draft to the calendar invite.
